digest.component_or_area: dependency advisory CI gating and escalation
propositions: Committed locks freeze transitive dependencies, causing any subsequent advisory on a pinned version to fail CI gates without code changes by affected authors.
The Gerrit verify gate now blocks on transitive-dependency advisories only when a change touches the dependency map (uv.lock, pyproject.toml, etc.), not when unrelated changes are in flight.
The scheduled main lane blocks releases on outstanding advisories by adding a gate to release.yml's authorize job, escalating via a daily canary that files and deduplicates alert tickets.

A severity-based blocking policy applies (CRITICAL/HIGH fail, MEDIUM warns, LOW tracked) with unrated advisories treated as HIGH, and override-dependencies is the documented escape hatch with required justification and REMOVE-WHEN markers.

The runbook pre-empts false-progress paths (constraint-dependencies UNSATISFIABLE being misread as proof of impossibility; uv lock --upgrade-package being a no-op against upstream caps) with explicit named guidance.
